page: Microsoft Azure E96-48s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, featuring AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. The configuration allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance provides 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding an elevated allocation of 14.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is included, requiring network-attached remote disks for persistent data. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Benchmark evaluations indicate upper-quartile memory throughput, achieving 263.69 GB/sec in read operations and 128.61 GB/sec in write operations across large 256 MB blocks. The instance registers a PassMark memory score of 2850.91 and demonstrated top-quartile performance in database operations with a score of 23498.42, alongside high encryption test throughput of 43888.24. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput also place in the upper quartile. Conversely, general raw compute tasks such as single-core stress-ng (1900.19) and Geekbench multi-core (15621.0) perform in the middle 50 percent tier.

The constrained compute architecture matches an extensive 672 GB memory footprint with half the active CPU cores of a full 96-vCPU footprint, optimizing cost efficiency for memory-bound applications where software licensing is tied to per-core counts. The absence of local disk requires external storage management over network channels. This hardware configuration is suited for memory-intensive workloads including large in-memory databases, high-capacity caching layers, memory-constrained data analytics pipelines, and data processing tasks requiring high memory bandwidth.
description: The Microsoft Azure E96-48s_v5 is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores and features a substantial 672.0 GB memory capacity, equivalent to 14.0 GB per vCPU. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and does not bundle local storage, relying on external disk options. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the upper 25 percent for uncached memory read and write bandwidth, database operations, PassMark memory performance, and hardware encryption tasks. Meanwhile, raw CPU metrics such as single-core and multi-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores align with the middle 50 percent benchmark tier. Due to its constrained CPU-to-memory design, this server offers resource efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, making it technically suitable for in-memory databases, extensive caching layers, and large-scale data analytics workloads requiring high memory density relative to core count.
